proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. Virchow2 is clearly the strongest single model (0.862) and prefers very strong regularisation (C=1e-4). UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 are weaker (0.81-0.83) and prefer C=0.1 with PCA 32-64. Metadata adds little.
REASONING: Start exploration with late_tuned using learned_weights. Every member runs at its own tuned setting, and the inner-CV weights can fall back to Virchow2 alone. This gives a robust anchor that shows whether the weaker models add complementary signal, before I map the shared-knob methods (early, late, gated).
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.865-0.875 AUROC, a small gain over Virchow2. If it is at or below 0.862, the other models add little beyond Virchow2 under probability-level fusion. Fusion gains would then have to come from early_tuned block weighting or not at all.

ANALYSIS: Virchow2 (Prism slide embedding) is the strongest single model at 0.862. late_tuned with learned_weights reached 0.855, below Virchow2 alone. Inner-CV weight selection on 134 patients is probably noisy and sometimes moves weight away from Virchow2. Lepidic and Papillary are the weakest classes.
REASONING: Exploration should map each method. early_tuned keeps each member's tuned PCA and learns block weights, so it can treat Virchow2 at its strong-shrinkage setting and give the others smaller weights. With members at PCA 32/32/64 plus meta, there are about 130 features, so a moderate C fits. Virchow2 alone used C=1e-4 on PCA32, but the shared C combines with the block weights. I choose C=0.01 and meta_weight=1 as a middle setting.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.86-0.875 if the complementary UNI/H-optimus blocks help Papillary and Lepidic. If it stays at or below 0.855, joint fusion with learned block weights adds little beyond Virchow2. In that case I would test a stronger C (0.001) or simple averaging with late_tuned mean_logit.

ANALYSIS: Both tuned fusions (learned_weights 0.855, early_tuned 0.847) fall short of the virchow2+meta baseline (0.862). Learned weights probably have noisy inner-CV weight selection on 134 patients. Virchow2's Prism slide embedding dominates, and its best C is very small (1e-4). The other members are tuned at C=0.1, which may make them overconfident.
REASONING: Still exploring. The untested late_tuned combiners need a check, and mean_logit is the simplest one with no inner-CV noise. Averaging logits of differently calibrated members tests whether plain ensembling adds diversity beyond Virchow2. It is cheap and answers whether combining tuned members helps at all.
EXPECTED: If mean_logit reaches about 0.865-0.875, the members are complementary and the earlier failure came from noisy learned weights. If it stays at or below 0.86, the UNI/H-optimus signal is redundant with Virchow2 or poorly calibrated. In that case I would try stacking with strong shrinkage, or early fusion with balance_blocks and small C.

ANALYSIS: Virchow2 alone (0.862) is the strongest member. Tuned late fusion with learned weights (0.855) and with mean_logit (0.840) both fall below it, and so does tuned early fusion (0.847). Pulling in UNI2-h and H-optimus seems to dilute Virchow2 rather than add complementary signal, at least under the tuned per-model settings. The untuned early, late and gated methods have not been tested yet.
REASONING: The exploration phase should cover the untested methods. Early fusion with balance_blocks=true and PCA 32 per model stops any one model from dominating through its column count, and strong shrinkage suits 167 patients. The tuned Virchow2 member needed C=1e-4 while the other two used 0.1, so in a shared standardised space a mid-range C=0.001 is a reasonable first probe. Keeping meta_weight=1 avoids overweighting age/sex, which was weak on its own (0.600).
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.85–0.87. If it lands well below Virchow2 alone, joint linear fusion of these embeddings is not adding signal, and I would next check late fusion with stacking and the gated method before concentrating on Virchow2-weighted variants.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far scores below virchow2 alone (0.862). Late_tuned with learned_weights gets 0.855, close to its single-best special case. Early fusion with PCA32, balanced blocks and C=0.001 gets 0.856, and early_tuned 0.847. So adding UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 seems to add noise. Virchow2 (a slide encoder) wants very strong regularisation (C=1e-4), and the shared C=0.001 may be too loose for it.
REASONING: Gated and the late stack combiner are still untested. Stacking on inner-CV log-probabilities can learn per-class reliance on each model, for example using UNI or H-optimus only where they help (Papillary and Lepidic are weak). A strong stack penalty (stack_C=0.01) limits overfitting with 134 patients. late_tuned keeps each member at its own optimal setting.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.855-0.87. If it stays below virchow2, per-class complementarity is too weak to exploit at this sample size, and later trials should go to stronger-regularised early fusion (C=1e-4, PCA16) or gated.

ANALYSIS: So far no fusion beats virchow2 alone (0.862). The best fusion results are early with PCA32, balanced blocks and C=0.001 (0.856) and late_tuned learned_weights (0.855). Virchow2 is clearly the strongest member and works best under very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4). Adding the weaker UNI/H-optimus members seems to dilute it, and the per-class profiles of all fusions are broadly similar.
REASONING: The gated method is untested and the exploration phase is meant to map every method. One gated trial with strong regularisation is the best use of this slot: hidden 32, dropout 0.5, weight decay 0.1, PCA 32, 200 epochs, lr 0.001, 3 seeds. A per-patient gate could in principle lean on Virchow2 while still drawing on the other models where they help. Early-fusion C variants can be tested later.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.83-0.86 AUROC, likely with larger fold SD from overfitting on 134 patients. If it lands clearly below 0.85, I will drop gated and concentrate on early fusion with Virchow2-favouring regularisation (lower C, block weights).

ANALYSIS: No fusion beats virchow2 alone (0.862). The best fusions are early with balanced blocks, PCA32 and C=0.001 (0.856) and late_tuned learned_weights (0.855). In early_tuned at C=0.01, Virchow2 is probably under-regularised compared with its tuned C=1e-4, and the weaker UNI/H-opt members dilute its signal. Papillary (0.72-0.75) and Lepidic (~0.78) are the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: Virchow2 alone prefers very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4). For early fusion, the open question is whether stronger regularisation plus L2 normalisation helps. The search space is unmapped for the late method with a shared C, and for early without balancing or with different C. A cheap informative probe is early with balance_blocks and C=0.0001, which matches Virchow2's own optimum. This tests whether the fusion simply needs heavier shrinkage. I keep PCA 32 and meta_weight 1 so this is a single-knob change from #4.
EXPECTED: If heavier shrinkage helps, AUROC should reach about 0.865-0.87, above virchow2 alone. If it drops or stays near 0.856, C=0.001 is near the optimum for early fusion, and I would next explore late (shared settings) with mean_prob or a larger PCA.

ANALYSIS: Virchow2 alone (0.862) is still ahead of every fusion. The best fusions are early with balanced blocks and PCA32 (0.856 at C=0.001 and C=0.0001) and late_tuned learned_weights (0.855). Every fusion improves Cribriform and Micropapillary but loses on Lepidic and Papillary. Strong regularisation suits Virchow2 (its tuned C is 0.0001), and the shared-setting late method has not been tested.
REASONING: This uses an exploration slot to map the untested 'late' family. It runs one shared, strongly regularised setting (C=0.001, PCA32) with plain mean_prob averaging. Mean_prob avoids the noisy inner-CV weight or stack fitting that hurt trials #3 and #5. Meta_weight=3 copies the setting that suited Virchow2.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.85–0.86, with smoother probabilities from equal averaging and possibly better Lepidic and Papillary. If it lands at or below 0.85, then averaging in the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 dilutes Virchow2. Gains would then have to come from early fusion that keeps Virchow2 dominant, such as early_tuned with lower C, rather than from late combination.

ANALYSIS: No fusion beats virchow2 alone (0.862): the best fusions are early with balanced PCA-32 blocks (0.856, flat between C=1e-4 and 1e-3), late_tuned learned_weights (0.855) and late mean_prob (0.853). Stacking and mean_logit are clearly worse. Papillary (~0.74) and Lepidic (~0.78) are the weak classes in every method, which suggests the weaker members (mainly uni2h) dilute virchow2's signal rather than add to it.
REASONING: early_tuned at C=0.01 put the virchow2 block at an inverse strength 100x weaker than its tuned 1e-4, which is probably why it scored only 0.847. At C=0.001 with meta_weight=3 (virchow2's tuned metadata weight), virchow2 sits much closer to its optimum. The inner-CV block weights can still shrink or drop uni2h and H-optimus. This tests whether keeping each member's own preprocessing, with virchow2 dominant, can exceed early's equal-block fusion.
EXPECTED: Expected AUROC about 0.86-0.87, with better Papillary and Lepidic if uni2h is down-weighted. If it stays at or below 0.856, block re-weighting under one shared C cannot recover virchow2's advantage. I would then focus on early and late variants: L2 normalisation, pca=16, and non-balanced blocks.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far scores 0.83-0.857 AUROC, below Virchow2+meta alone (0.862). The best fusions are early_tuned (C=0.001, meta=3: 0.8565), early with balanced PCA-32 blocks (0.856) and late_tuned learned_weights (0.855). Stacking and mean_logit hurt, likely because the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 members dilute Virchow2. Papillary (about 0.74) and Lepidic (about 0.78) are the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: Virchow2 does best under very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4, meta_weight=3). In early_tuned, Virchow2 gets its own setting only if the global C is 1e-4. The learned block weights can then down-weight or drop the other blocks. Going from C=1e-3 to 1e-4 already raised early AUROC from 0.8563 to 0.8556 with a lower SD (0.027), so stronger shrinkage looks harmless and may stabilise the fit. This last exploration trial tests whether a Virchow2-anchored early fusion can match or beat the best single model.
EXPECTED: AUROC of about 0.858-0.866 with a lower fold SD. If it stays at or below 0.857, then shrinkage is not what holds early fusion back. The other models would add little beyond Virchow2 under linear fusion. The next step would be targeted per-class gains, for example late fusion with weights that favour Virchow2, rather than more C tuning.

proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: No fusion has beaten Virchow2 alone (0.862). The best fusions are early, early_tuned and late learned_weights, all at about 0.855-0.857. Strong regularisation (C=1e-4 to 1e-3) with PCA=32 is consistently best. Stacking and mean_logit hurt, and the gated network did not help. Papillary (~0.74) and Lepidic (~0.77) are the weak classes for every method.
REASONING: Per-slide L2 normalisation has never been tested in any trial. It could change the geometry of the UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 mean-of-tile embeddings, which are the weaker members that may be diluting Virchow2. To isolate that effect, this trial is a one-knob change from #7 (early, pca=32, meta_weight=1, C=1e-4, balance_blocks=True), which had the lowest fold SD.
EXPECTED: If L2 normalisation helps, AUROC should rise to about 0.865 or more, with gains in Acinar, Papillary or Lepidic. If the result stays within ±0.005 of #7, L2 normalisation is irrelevant after standardising. In that case I will instead reduce the weaker models' influence, for example by trying pca=16 or late_tuned mean_prob.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far lands at 0.853-0.858 AUROC, slightly below Virchow2 alone (0.862). Virchow2 is the strongest and most stable member, and adding UNI2-h/H-optimus-1 seems to dilute it rather than add complementary signal. Strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) gives the lowest fold SD, and L2 normalisation and meta_weight give only noise-level changes.
REASONING: Balanced blocks with PCA 32 force equal influence from the weaker models. Early fusion without PCA and without balance_blocks lets Virchow2's 2560 columns carry most of the variance, so it dominates while the others still contribute small corrections under heavy shrinkage. This tests directly whether the losses come from equalising the models. l2_normalize=True and meta_weight=3 match the best settings seen so far.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.862-0.870, with Papillary and Lepidic closer to Virchow2's level. If it stays at about 0.857 or lower, the weaker models' features are simply adding noise. In that case I would test late_tuned mean_prob or learned_weights-style schemes that can nearly drop them.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.846-0.860 AUROC. None clearly beats Virchow2 alone (0.862). The best fusion so far is trial #12: early, L2 normalisation, no PCA, C=0.0001, at 0.8595, but it was rejected as noise. Heavy shrinkage (C=0.0001) consistently gives the lowest fold SD and the best balanced accuracy. Stacking and mean_logit hurt, probably because the weaker UNI2-h member drags them down.
REASONING: The most promising region is early fusion of the full L2-normalised embeddings. That setup keeps Virchow2's 2560 columns, so it has the largest raw share. Only C=0.0001 has been tested there. Moving one step to C=0.001 tells us whether the strong-shrinkage optimum is real, or whether less shrinkage lets the complementary Cribriform, Micropapillary and Solid signal from H-optimus/UNI add information.
EXPECTED: If AUROC rises to about 0.863-0.866 with similar SD, it may clear the threshold of about 0.004 over #10, and I would then refine meta_weight or balance_blocks around it. If it falls back to about 0.855, C=0.0001 is the optimum in this region. That would mean fusion is effectively capped near Virchow2 alone, and I would test balance_blocks=False against PCA variants or late fusion with learned weights at strong shrinkage.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants plateau at 0.846-0.860 AUROC, essentially tied with Virchow2 alone (0.862). The best results come from heavy shrinkage (C=1e-4 to 1e-3), L2 normalisation and no PCA, where Virchow2's 2560 columns dominate. Accepted gains are tiny (0.001-0.003), well below the thresholds. Late fusion so far used only moderate settings: C=0.001 with PCA 32, or the tuned members, whose UNI and H-optimus members sit at C=0.1.
REASONING: One open question is whether late fusion improves when every member uses the same strongly shrunk, full-dimension, L2-normalised representation that worked best for early fusion. mean_logit with well-regularised members could cut variance in weak classes such as Papillary and Lepidic without letting the weaker models' overfitting leak in. This tests a different fusion mechanism in the best-known regime, rather than tuning another early variant by a few thousandths.
EXPECTED: AUROC of about 0.86-0.87, possibly with better Papillary and Lepidic AUROC. If it lands at or below 0.86, I will conclude that UNI2 and H-optimus add little beyond Virchow2 under any combination rule. The remaining budget would then go to a few targeted checks, such as meta_weight=10 or a stronger gated regularisation, before accepting the plateau.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants plateau at 0.855-0.860 AUROC, at or just below virchow2 alone (0.862). The best runs are early concatenations with strong shrinkage (C=1e-4). Unbalanced full-dimensional blocks (#12, 0.8595) beat PCA-32 balanced blocks. That suggests letting Virchow2's many columns dominate the logistic regression helps. Late and stacking combiners are consistently worse, likely because the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 members dilute Virchow2.
REASONING: #12 is the closest to a gain over the current best (#10). The open question is whether its gain comes from L2 normalisation or from the unreduced, unbalanced blocks. Dropping L2 normalisation while keeping the full dimensions, no balancing and C=1e-4 isolates that knob. It also keeps Virchow2 (2560 of 5632 columns) as the dominant block. It is the cheapest plausible route to a small but clear gain, at a strong shrinkage setting.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.858-0.862 AUROC. It probably stays below the acceptance threshold, but it would tell us whether L2 normalisation matters. If it lands at or below 0.857, then L2 normalisation was helping. In that case I would try l2=True with pca=128, or meta_weight=10, before concluding that fusion cannot beat Virchow2 alone.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far lands at 0.847-0.860 AUROC, none clearly above the accepted best #10 (0.857). All sit at or below Virchow2 alone (0.862). Early fusion with very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4, no PCA, L2 on) gives the highest numbers, but the gains of +0.001 to +0.003 are within noise. Late combiners and stacking are worse. Gated was tried only once (0.8475) at a moderately regularised setting.
REASONING: More tweaks to early C, meta_weight or L2 have already shown differences below the threshold, so they waste budget. The only family that could plausibly add something qualitatively different is gated, a per-patient model weighting that could down-weight UNI2-h where it is noisy. Its single trial was likely under-regularised for 134 training patients. This trial tightens it on every axis: L2 per slide, smaller PCA, a 16-d projection, heavy weight decay and fewer epochs. That tests whether gated can match or beat strongly shrunk early fusion.
EXPECTED: If the earlier gated result was limited by overfitting, AUROC should rise to about 0.86-0.87, with smaller fold SD and gains in Acinar and Papillary. If it stays at or below about 0.855, I conclude gating adds nothing at this sample size. I would then drop gated and spend the remaining few trials confirming that fusion cannot clearly beat Virchow2 alone, e.g. late_tuned mean_prob.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion method has plateaued at about 0.855-0.860 AUROC, still below virchow2 alone (0.862). Strongly regularised early fusion (C 1e-4 to 1e-3) is the most stable family. Late averaging of tuned members and gating are worse, which suggests UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 add mostly redundant or noisy signal on top of Virchow2. Varying L2 normalisation, balance_blocks and PCA None/32 changed the score by only about 0.001-0.003.
REASONING: PCA=16 per model in early fusion is still untested. It is a different noise-reduction approach from heavy L2 shrinkage: each model keeps only its dominant axes, which may capture the morphology signal while dropping the high-dimensional noise from the weaker models. A smaller total dimension also tolerates a milder C (1e-3). balance_blocks keeps the three blocks equal, and meta_weight=3 matches the best settings so far. I am not retrying late_tuned averaging: the heavily regularised virchow2 member gives flat probabilities that equal-weight averaging would swamp.
EXPECTED: An AUROC of about 0.86-0.87, with possible gains on Papillary and Lepidic, the weakest classes. If it fails to clear the threshold, early fusion is saturated with respect to dimensionality. I would then conclude fusion offers no reliable gain over virchow2 alone, and spend the remaining trials sparingly (e.g. stack with a larger stack_C) rather than chasing noise.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far sits between 0.847 and 0.860 AUROC. The accepted best is early_tuned (#10, 0.8570), which is still below virchow2 alone (0.8624). Early-fusion variants (L2, PCA, C, balance_blocks) differ by less than the paired threshold, so that region looks saturated. Late fusion with tuned members was hurt by combining on raw scale: mean_logit scored 0.840 and stack at stack_C=0.01 scored 0.830. A likely cause is that virchow2's member runs at C=0.0001 and gives near-flat probabilities, which equal-weight averaging dilutes.
REASONING: Stacking is the only combiner that can rescale each member's log-probabilities per class, which undoes the scale mismatch between the C=0.0001 virchow2 member and the C=0.1 members. At stack_C=0.01 the second-level model was probably over-shrunk and could not learn those scales. stack_C=0.1 tests whether a less-regularised stacker can exploit the complementary per-class strengths. Examples: UNI/H-optimus fused models give higher Acinar AUROC in #1 and #8 (0.84 vs 0.82-0.83), and early fusion gives higher Cribriform. This is an open, plausibly high-gain question, unlike further small early-fusion tweaks.
EXPECTED: If scale mismatch was the problem, AUROC should rise to roughly 0.86-0.87 and clear the threshold over #10. If it stays at about 0.83-0.85, stacking on 134 patients is too noisy whatever its regularisation. In that case I will drop stack and probe the remaining untested combiners (weighted_vote) or a better-regularised gated net before concluding that fusion cannot beat virchow2.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has beaten Virchow2+meta (0.862). The best fusions are early, early_tuned and early with L2 at C=1e-4, all around 0.856-0.860, and their gains over #10 are below the threshold. Late fusion with fixed combiners (mean_logit, stack) loses accuracy. late_tuned learned_weights reached 0.855, but its members run at very different C values (Virchow2 at 1e-4, the others at 0.1), so their probabilities are not on comparable scales.
REASONING: Plain late fusion with learned_weights is untested. Using a shared C=1e-4, PCA 32, no L2 and meta_weight 3 makes the Virchow2 member identical to its tuned baseline. The UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 members then get equally strong shrinkage, so their probabilities sit on a similar scale to Virchow2's. Inner-CV simplex weights can then lean on Virchow2 and add a small share of the others where they help. This avoids the scale mismatch that hurt late_tuned.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.860-0.866 if learning the weights on a common scale works, possibly a clear gain over #10's 0.857. If it lands at or below about 0.857, that indicates inner-CV weight learning on 134 patients is too noisy. I would then conclude that fusion adds little beyond Virchow2 and use the remaining trials to probe early-fusion settings such as PCA 64/128 with L2 before stopping.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants plateau at 0.855-0.86 AUROC, essentially tied with virchow2+meta alone (0.8623). Strong shrinkage (C=1e-4 to 1e-3) is consistently best. Per-slide L2 and no PCA gave the best early result (#12, 0.8595). Late learned_weights at Virchow's tuned setting (#19, 0.8623) essentially reproduces the Virchow baseline. Stacking, gating and late_tuned with mixed C scales are clearly worse. In late_tuned, mean_logit is probably skewed by the very different logit scales of the members.
REASONING: Late fusion with learned_weights can never do much worse than the best member, because weight 1 on one model is allowed. Rerunning it in the L2-normalised, no-PCA regime that gave the best early fusion tests whether full-dimensional members carry complementary signal that the inner CV picks up. That would raise the weak Papillary and Lepidic classes. It is a different, untested point near the best region, not a tiny C or PCA tweak.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.860-0.866, with a possible gain over #10 of ~0.005 to 0.009, near the acceptance threshold. If it is not accepted, the conclusion is that the three encoders add no complementary information beyond Virchow2 at this sample size. I would then make only one or two more distinct probes, such as early_tuned with meta_weight=10, and accept the stop rule.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has cleared Virchow2 alone (0.8624). Early, early_tuned and late variants all plateau at 0.855-0.860. learned_weights at C=1e-4 reaches 0.862, probably by collapsing onto Virchow2. Stacking and gating overfit, and the gains are well below the noise thresholds. Every competitive configuration uses very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4), which is Virchow2's preferred setting.
REASONING: Only 5 non-improving trials remain before the stop rule. One open question is cheap to test: does plain equal-weight probability averaging help when all members run at the strong shrinkage that suits Virchow2? Late mean_prob has only been tried at C=1e-3 (#8, 0.853). learned_weights at C=1e-4 (#19) was the strongest fusion so far, so equal averaging at C=1e-4 checks whether UNI2/H-optimus add complementary signal (e.g. Acinar, Lepidic) rather than just noise.
EXPECTED: Probably ~0.855-0.865. A clear gain (>~0.01 over #10) would show that equal-weight ensembling adds value at strong regularisation. If the score is flat or lower, I conclude that the extra models mostly add noise relative to Virchow2. I would also conclude that fusion cannot reliably beat the best single-model baseline on this cohort, so the remaining trials should only test the last structurally different ideas before the stop rule ends the search.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.855-0.862, which is no better than Virchow2+meta alone (0.862). Learned-weight late fusion (#19, #20) reaches about 0.862, which suggests it mostly selects Virchow2. Stacking and the gated nets lose clearly. The best early variants (unregularised-scale C=0.0001, no PCA, L2 on, unbalanced, so Virchow2 dominates) give +0.001 to +0.003 over #10, all within noise.
REASONING: Four non-improving trials remain before the stop rule. The strongest early config (#12) leaves one knob near the region not tested: metadata weight. Age and sex are weak (AUROC 0.60), but they help some classes, such as In situ vs invasive patterns with age. At very strong shrinkage (C=0.0001), meta_weight=10 is the only way to keep them from being washed out. This is a cheap test of whether under-weighted metadata is what limits early fusion. Structural alternatives look worse. early_tuned cannot give UNI/H-optimus a weaker penalty than Virchow2's. late_tuned weighted_vote is unlikely to beat learned_weights.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC of about 0.858-0.862, which would be a rejection. If it is rejected, I conclude that fusion saturates at the Virchow2 level and that metadata weighting is not the bottleneck. The search should then end with the honest finding that no fusion clearly beats the best single model. A gain of more than 0.005 with low fold SD would mean metadata was being over-shrunk in early fusion.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has clearly beaten virchow2+meta (0.862). The current best is early_tuned at 0.857. The best late runs (learned_weights, 0.862) essentially reproduce virchow2 alone, which suggests the inner CV mostly selects Virchow2. Early fusion plateaus at 0.855-0.860 regardless of L2, PCA or block balancing. Gated and stacking are clearly worse.
REASONING: Only 3 trials remain before the stop rule. The best use is a low-variance paired comparison against #10. That means the same method with one changed knob, so the gain's SE and therefore the threshold stay small (~0.004). In early_tuned, raising meta_weight from 1 to 3 helped (#9 vs #2). Pushing it to 10 at the best C of 1e-4 is the last untested meta setting at that C, and it stays within the strongly regularised regime that suits Virchow2's tuned member.
EXPECTED: Expect 0.857-0.861: a small gain, likely under threshold. If it is not accepted, the conclusion is that fusion does not add detectable signal beyond Virchow2 (Prism2) on 167 patients. In that case the honest result is that the best single model, virchow2+meta, is not beaten.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has cleared the acceptance threshold. Linear early and late fusion plateau at about 0.855-0.862, which is the level of Virchow2+meta alone (0.8623). learned_weights reproduces exactly that, consistent with it simply selecting Virchow2. UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 seem to add little complementary signal under linear fusion. Stacking and heavily regularised gating did worse.
REASONING: Two trials remain before the stop rule, so another near-duplicate linear variant would only produce sub-threshold noise. The one mechanism that is structurally different and not yet fairly probed is the per-patient gate. Trial #6 (PCA 32, hidden 32, wd 0.1, 200 epochs) reached 0.8475. Trial #16 (PCA 16, wd 1.0) underfit at 0.824. This trial tries a moderate setting: L2 norm (which helped linear models), PCA 64 to keep more signal, hidden 64, strong dropout 0.5, mild weight decay 0.01, short training (100 epochs) to limit overfitting, and meta_weight 3, which suited Virchow2.
EXPECTED: If patient-specific weighting of the models helps (for example for Papillary or Lepidic, which all methods find hard), AUROC should exceed about 0.862 with a gain over #10 above the threshold. If it lands at or below about 0.85, I conclude the gate cannot be trained reliably on 134 patients per fold. Fusion then offers no reliable gain over Virchow2 alone, and the best single model should be kept.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has clearly beaten Virchow2+meta (0.8623). Early and early_tuned fusion plateau at 0.856-0.860 regardless of L2 normalisation, PCA, meta_weight or C. Stacking and gated networks overfit. learned_weights reaches about 0.862, essentially reproducing Virchow2 alone. UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 seem to add little information beyond Virchow2 at n=167.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule. learned_weights is the only combiner that matches the best single model, and it scored +0.005 over the current best (#10), but the threshold was 0.014. A less-shrunk member setting (C=0.001 with L2 normalisation, no PCA) could let UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 contribute complementary signal. That signal might lift Papillary and Lepidic, the weakest classes, enough for learned_weights to add real weight to those members. The trial also tests whether the learned weights stay collapsed on Virchow2.
EXPECTED: Most likely about 0.86, not accepted. That would mean fusion offers no detectable gain over Virchow2+meta under this protocol, and the single-model baseline should be preferred. If it reaches 0.875 or more with Papillary and Lepidic improving, the other members contribute when less regularised.
